p: Henwood sits on the eastern side of Ashford, close to the town centre and the A20, so it's a simple trip from the M20. It's also within walking distance of the centre if you're arriving at Ashford International by train.

Ashford has a quirky landmark that kids love: a real First World War tank stands in St George's Square. It was presented to the town after the war in recognition of its fundraising efforts, and it's now a protected piece of history. Don't miss it.

Victoria Park is the town's big green space, with play areas, sports pitches and the grand Victorian Hubert Fountain. Just outside town, Godinton House and Gardens is a historic house with formal gardens that's a calmer option for grown-ups.

If you want a bigger day out, Port Lympne Safari Park near Hythe is a short drive south, with safari trucks taking you among rhinos, giraffes and big cats. Head out across the flat landscape of Romney Marsh and you can reach the coast at Dymchurch, which is great fun for a bucket-and-spade afternoon.
Canterbury, with its famous cathedral and lovely old streets, is about twenty minutes up the road, and Leeds Castle near Maidstone is another popular day trip from Ashford.
Ashford grew up as a market town, and while it's modernised quickly, there's still a pleasant old core around St Mary's Church. It's worth a quick wander if you're in town anyway.
After a busy session, the town centre has plenty of places to eat, so feeding a hungry gang won't be a problem.
